items.summary: Scientists are inventing new ways to search for the missing mass of the universe. The post Novel Experiments Expand the Hunt for ‘Ultralight’ Dark Matter first appeared on Quanta Magazine

items.title: Oscillatory integral operators of arbitrary signature: beyond the universal estimates
items.summary: We consider H\"ormander oscillatory integral operators on $\mathbb{R}^n$. In particular, we are interested in proving bounds with dependence on the signature of the phase. The sharp universal range of $L^p\to L^p$ estimates was obtained for any given signature by the second author and Iliopoulou. Under the mild non-compression hypotheses on the phase introduced in Chen et al., we prove $L^p\to L^p$ estimates that go beyond this universal range in odd dimensions. We also obtain the sharp universal range of $L^p\to L^q$ estimates for odd $n$. The techniques are based on the breakthrough work of Wang--Wu on the Fourier restriction conjecture.

items.title: Relativistic Hydrodynamics as an Intersection Problem
items.summary: Ideal relativistic hydrodynamics admits a covariant description as an intersection problem in a symplectic space associated with spacetime. The independent fields are differential forms of degrees 0,1,3,4. Spacetime diffeomorphisms and shifts of the momentum one-form act Hamiltonianly; the zero locus of their moment map is a coisotropic subvariety encoding the transport equations. The spacetime metric and equation of state determine a Lagrangian submanifold, whose intersection with the coisotropic subvariety is precisely the Lichnerowicz--Carter system. We explain the geometric meaning of the canonical flow parameter, derive circulation and Ertel invariants directly from the constraints…

items.title: ACT Excited: Reconciling Starobinsky and Quadratic Chaotic Inflationary Models with ACT Results via Excited States
items.summary: Data Release 6 of the Atacama Cosmology Telescope, combined with Planck, CMB lensing and DESI BAO data, favours a higher scalar spectral index $n_{s}$ than Planck and a mildly positive running $\alpha_{s}$, putting the Starobinsky model in tension with the data, while the quadratic chaotic model is already excluded by its large tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$. We show that relaxing the Bunch--Davies assumption for the initial state of the scalar perturbations can restore agreement without modifying the inflaton potential. Parametrising the Bogoliubov coefficients by an excitation parameter $\chi_{S}$ and a relative phase $2\varphi_{S}$, we derive the shifts of $n_{s}$ and $\alpha_{s}$ induced…

items.title: Analytical solution of general interface problems for reaction-advection-diffusion equations
items.summary: We obtain novel integral representations, expressed as contour integrals in the complex Fourier plane, for the solution of fully nonhomogeneous interface problems for classical reaction-advection-diffusion (RAD) equations with arbitrary initial data on the line and general interface conditions at the origin. Such problems of applied mathematics emerge in a spectacular variety of physical phenomena in mathematical physics, chemistry, continuum mechanics, biology, pharmacokinetics, as well as mathematical finance. A suitable implementation of Fokas' unified transform method is in force herein, with particular challenges arising due to inclusion in the model of lower-order terms, and the…

items.title: Imprints of quantum space in the ringdown phase of Kerr black holes
items.summary: We investigate quantum-space corrections to the gravitational quasinormal modes (QNMs) of Kerr black holes within the framework of noncommutative geometry. The analysis employs a pseudo-semi-Killing Drinfeld twist, which preserves the classical Kerr geometry as an exact background solution while introducing nontrivial quantum corrections to linearized gravitational perturbations. Working to first order in the black hole spin and the quantum deformation parameter, including their mixed contribution, we derive a Schr\"odinger-like master equation for axial gravitational perturbations with a frequency- and spin-dependent effective potential. We compute the fundamental QNM frequencies using…

items.title: The Generalized Second Law from Fluctuation Theorems in a Quantum Reference Frame
items.summary: We prove the generalized second law (GSL) for black-hole exteriors undergoing unitary driving and relaxation on a fixed semifinite algebra. Wall's influential proof assumes semiclassical geometry and restricts fixed parent states to algebras of successive horizon cuts. We instead evolve the state on a fixed dressed exterior algebra. With complete characteristic data, the same semiclassical exterior supports both descriptions, analogous to the Heisenberg and Schr\"odinger pictures through state--operator duality. Using a gravitational charge as a quantum clock, we construct a modular crossed product with density operators whose trace entropy reproduces generalized entropy up to clock…

items.title: Symmetry breaking Poincar{\'e}--Einstein metrics and non-extendable boundary Killing fields
items.summary: We construct Poincar{\'e}-Einstein metrics on $R^2xS^3xS^2xS^2$ which bifurcate from anti-de Sitter black holes whose horizon is the product of a B{\"o}hm metric on $S^3xS^2$ with a round $S^2$ , and which break the rotational symmetry of the $S^2$ factor while keeping their conformal infinity. Some Killing fields of the conformal infinity therefore do not extend to the bulk, although $$\pi$^1(M, $\partial$M ) = 0$. The construction rests on two results of independent interest: the Lichnerowicz eigenvalues of B{\"o}hm metrics on invariant transverse traceless tensors are simple (with at most two exceptional values), the lowest one tends to $-$\infty$$ along B{\"o}hm's sequence with a gap…

items.title: Near-boundary and near-horizon momentum--Krylov response in noncommutative-inspired BTZ spacetime
items.summary: We compute the proper radial momentum of a massive probe falling into a Lorentzian-smeared, noncommutative-inspired BTZ black hole at fixed asymptotic mass, and use it as the growth rate of momentum--Krylov complexity. In the BTZ limit the accumulated complexity is $\mathcal{K}_0 = X(\cosh\tau - 1)$. With smearing, the initial growth coefficient is $F'_\alpha(X)/4$, while the late-time exponent is the surface gravity $F'_\alpha(x_+)/2$. The two depend differently on the smearing parameter, so the deformed response is not a rescaled BTZ curve; we show this analytically and confirm it numerically. For a distant release point the early response approaches BTZ, whereas the late-time rate does…

items.title: Quadratic-in-spin scattering of compact bodies at fourth post-Minkowskian order
items.summary: We present the fourth-post-Minkowskian scattering angle of aligned spinning compact bodies through quadratic spin at arbitrary velocity and mass ratio. We include spin-induced quadrupoles and radiation reaction, supplemented by curvature-squared spin-tidal terms. Three-loop worldline integrals yield closed forms in polylogarithms and elliptic integrals. Infrared poles cancel exactly, fixing the tail logarithm. We obtain a new post-Newtonian coefficient and third-order angular-momentum loss for general quadrupoles. The new input shifts resummed predictions for black-hole scattering.

items.title: Void inside the horizon: connecting the third-quantized vacuum to a classical spacetime
items.summary: We investigate the emergence of a classical spacetime from a quantum-gravitational vacuum within the framework of third quantization applied to the black hole interior. Following the canonical quantization of the Kantowski--Sachs spacetime, one can construct a wave packet that explains the classical interior of a Schwarzschild black hole. This wave packet should be extended to the classical singularity. To avoid this, one can introduce an analytic continuation and the Euclidean wave function. This is not an analytic continuation of the spacetime, but of the superspace. To give this a suitable meaning, it is reasonable to introduce the concept of the third quantization. In this aspect, the…

items.title: Exotic Universal Covers and Free Cyclic Actions from the Cartwright-Steger Surface
items.summary: For every $m\geq2$, we construct a closed minimal symplectic four-manifold with fundamental group $\Z/m$, Euler characteristic $35$, and signature $1$. The construction is a genus-five symplectic sum of a blowup of the regular fourfold Cartwright-Steger cover and a cyclic Akhmedov-Park manifold. The gluing identifies the homomorphisms from the two surface groups to $\Z/m$. The universal cover is minimal symplectic and is homeomorphic but not diffeomorphic to $(18m-1)\CP\#(17m-1)\CPb$. It admits a free symplectic action of $\Z/m$. Intermediate quotients give examples with fundamental group $\Z/n$ and characteristic numbers $(e,\sigma)=(35k,k)$ for every $n\geq2$ and $k\geq1$. Using the same…

items.title: Primordial black holes production in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity
items.summary: We consider models with the Gauss-Bonnet term multiplied to a function of the scalar field and propose a new inflationary model which provides a mechanism for the formation of primordial black holes (PBHs). For certain values of the model parameters, the predictions of this model agree with observational data from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT). Due to estimation of possiable PBHs masses, we demonstrate that they can be considered as a possible source for all or part of dark matter.

items.title: Boundary spectroscopy of hidden near-horizon reflection
items.summary: A classical black hole horizon absorbs completely, and any deviation would be hidden in the bulk. For a scalar field in a rotating Ba\~nados-Teitelboim-Zanelli exterior, we derive an exact boundary response of a corotating passive wall near the horizon. An Airy filter gives its spectrum, and positive energy excludes growing modes. On any frequency band the response identifies a constant wall impedance and the wall position, which enter orthogonally with weights determined by the spectral function. The boundary thus sees a reflecting wall, whereas a perfect absorber is exponentially hidden.

items.title: Dissipative Tidal Love Numbers of Neutron Stars from Viscous Heating
items.summary: We compute the leading low-frequency dissipative tidal response of nonrotating relativistic neutron stars. We formulate the response in a worldline effective field theory. We determine the linear dissipative Love number in two complementary ways: from the redshifted viscous entropy production inside the star and from the imaginary, frequency-odd part of the exterior metric. The first method reduces the calculation to an integral over the static equilibrium tide; the second provides an independent check. We apply our approach to publicly available equations of state and assess the corresponding correction to the gravitational-wave phase of neutron-star binaries. For an equal-mass…

items.title: Chiral and deconfinement thermodynamics of the Polyakov-quark linear sigma model with and without charm quark: an SU(3) versus SU(4) comparison
items.summary: Using the Polyakov-loop extended linear-sigma model (PLSM), we investigate strongly interacting matter at finite temperature and baryon density by comparing the three-flavor (u,d,s) and four-flavor (u,d,s,c) formulations on equal footing, with the aim of isolating the thermal contribution of the charm quark. The model describes chiral dynamics through explicit and spontaneous symmetry breaking and reproduces the vacuum spectra of scalar and pseudoscalar mesons. Confinement is incorporated through a logarithmic Polyakov-loop potential calibrated to the continuum lattice-QCD equation of state (EoS). Within the mean-field approximation, we calculate light-, strange-, and charm-quark…

items.title: Spin-geodesic systems
items.summary: We introduce and study a class of geometric dynamical systems on Riemannian manifolds called spin-geodesic systems, in which the motion of a point is coupled to an internal classical spin through a symmetric endomorphism field $B$, the spin-coupling field. These systems may be viewed as $B$-dependent deformations of geodesic motion and have connections with frame flows, magnetic geodesic flows, and nonholonomic rolling systems. We show that every spin-geodesic system admits an equivalent interpretation as a no-slip rolling system in an abstract ambient geometry; when the associated metric connection, determined by $B$, is flat, this construction reduces, under the usual integrability…

items.title: Spin-Torsion Coupling: Vector and Scalar Torsional Potentials of Chiral Spinor Currents
items.summary: We investigate integral representations of torsional fields sourced by chiral spinor currents within a weak-field, Ricci-flow-inspired geometric framework. Starting from the coupling between spinorial currents and axial torsion, we construct screened Green-kernel solutions and examine their relation to antisymmetric tetradic perturbations and contorsion. Particular attention is devoted to stationary toroidal configurations, for which the magnetic-type dipole moment vanishes while a nonzero toroidal moment and effective circulation remain. The dependence of these quantities on Yukawa screening is analyzed, together with their implications for an Aharonov-Bohm-like geometric structure. We…

items.title: Polynomial mixing for 2D Ising with plus boundary conditions
items.summary: We study the Glauber dynamics of the 2D Ising model at low temperatures. In the absence of boundary conditions, the mixing time on an $n\times n$ box is exponential in $n$ due to a bottleneck between metastable plus and minus phases. When the symmetry is broken via all-plus boundary conditions, it has been predicted in the physics literature since work of Lifshitz (1962) that from an all-minus initialization, the minus droplet shrinks via mean-curvature flow on timescales that are quadratic in $n$, and thus, the system equilibrates in polynomial time. On the rigorous side, the strongest result was a quasi-polynomial mixing time upper bound due to Lubetzky, Martinelli, Sly and Toninelli…

items.title: Rotating Black Holes from Scaling Transformations in Horava Gravity
items.summary: We study the scaling transformations that change the physical parameters of solutions in low-energy Horava gravity. In particular, we present a simple scaling transformation that generates rotating black-hole solutions in low-energy Horava gravity from known relativistic solutions. As explicit examples, we obtain "Doran-like" and "Kerr-Schild-like" rotating solutions in Horava gravity. We find that both solutions are horizon-penetrating, but their null horizons are not Killing horizons. We also find that, although their singularity structures differ from each other, chronology is protected in both solutions, as in the previously obtained Kerr-like solutions in Boyer-Lindquist coordinates.

items.title: The index from a super-point
items.summary: We extend the algebro-geometric construction of filtered graded rings that encode both the Higgs branch and the Macdonald index of 4d $\mathcal{N}=2$ superconformal field theories to theories whose Schur sector contains fermionic generators. The rings are then $\mathbb{Z}_2$-graded-commutative, and the index is reproduced by the Hilbert series of a generalized arc space, whose defining ideal may contain relations among the generators and their derivatives. We study the free $\mathcal{N}=2$ vector multiplet, $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang--Mills with gauge algebras $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ and $\mathfrak{su}(3)$, the rank-one $\mathcal{N}=3$ SCFTs, and the $\widehat{E}_6(SU(2))$ SCFT. For the…

items.title: Periods, isomonodromy, and modularity of ALG/ALG$^*$ gravitational instantons
items.summary: We prove that every smooth ALG or ALG$^*$ gravitational instanton of type $A_0,A_1,A_2,D_0,D_1,D_2,D_3$ is, up to homothety and hyperk\"ahler rotation, isometric to a rank-two wild Hitchin moduli space on $\PP^1$ with its $L^2$ metric. We compute the compact hyperk\"ahler periods and asymptotic parameters of these moduli spaces and give explicit inverse formulas for every admissible choice of these data. For the three ALG types, global isomonodromic transport realizes the two real parameters left undetermined by the compact periods. We use a Hamiltonian variation formula and uniform comparison with the semiflat metric to apply the Torelli and uniqueness theorems.

items.title: Classification of Chern-Simons Couplings and Deformed Pull-Backs on D-Branes
items.summary: We establish a framework for classifying higher-derivative Ramond-Ramond (RR) couplings on Dp-branes, focusing on the complete scattering amplitude of a closed-string RR state, a gauge field, and two transverse scalars. The low-energy expansion reveals infinite massless poles and local interaction terms, surpassing standard Myers and Taylor expansions. We propose a higher-class deformation of the pullback using mixed Chern-Simons transgression operators to address these complexities. Our three conjectures are as follows: 1. For fixed field content and derivative order, effective couplings form a finite-dimensional space under stated equivalences. 2. A family of mixed RR, gauge, and scalar…

items.title: All-Order Linearized Hydrodynamics of Charged Holographic Plasmas
items.summary: We investigate linearized all-order transport in a finite-density holographic plasma described by five-dimensional Einstein-Maxwell-Chern-Simons theory. By retaining the full frequency- and momentum-dependence of the fluid/gravity equations, we determine generalized shear, diffusion, higher-gradient, and chiral-vortical transport functions together with their real-time memory kernels. The different channels exhibit a clear hierarchy of temporal response: the leading shear and diffusion sectors respond promptly, whereas the higher-gradient sectors develop only after a finite buildup time. Remarkably, the chiral-vortical response also shows a finite buildup time despite entering at first…

items.title: The Sensitivity of Higgs Factories to the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model via Precision Measurements
items.summary: Precision measurements of Higgs boson couplings at future Higgs factories provide an indirect probe of new particles at mass scales beyond the reach of the high luminosity run of the Large Hadron Collider (HL-LHC). We study this sensitivity in the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (MSSM), focusing on radiative corrections to the third-generation Yukawa couplings. In particular, supersymmetric threshold corrections to the bottom Yukawa coupling and, in a smaller parameter region, to the tau Yukawa coupling, can remain significant even for multi-TeV superpartner masses. We perform a numerical survey of the MSSM parameter space, using a Markov Chain Monte Carlo, in order to identify…

items.title: Holographic Mutual Information in an Anisotropic Field Theory
items.summary: We investigate holographic mutual information in an anisotropic strongly coupled plasma within the framework of gauge/gravity duality. Considering both parallel and perpendicular strip configurations, we analyze the effects of temperature, anisotropy, strip lengths, and separation distance on the correlation structure between subsystems. For strips with equal lengths, we show that increasing temperature suppresses mutual information and reduces the size of the correlated region in the phase diagram. We find that the parallel configuration exhibits a monotonic behavior. However, the perpendicular configuration displays a more complex behavior resulting from the competition between the…

items.title: Initial Conditions and Wave-Phase Resolution for Scalar-Field Dark Matter Simulations
items.summary: Wave-based cosmological simulations of scalar-field dark matter (SFDM) require accurate initialization of both density and complex-wavefunction phase. We develop and validate a matched $\Lambda$CDM--SFDM initialization framework connecting CLASS-SFDM, MUSIC, and AxioNyx. For quadratic SFDM with $m_\phi=3.1623\times10^{-22}\,\mathrm{eV}$ at $z_{\rm ini}=120$, the scalar-component half-power scale is $k_{50}^{\phi}\simeq10.54\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$. An independent AxiECAMB comparison gives a normalized RMS deviation of $0.328\%$ in the synchronous-gauge SFDM velocity divergence over $0.20944\leq k\leq13.4\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$. items.title: Prospects for Detecting Post-merger Signals from Binary Neutron Stars with Future Gravitational-Wave Detectors
items.summary: The post-merger (PM) phase of binary neutron star (BNS) mergers carries information about the merger remnant and the dense-matter equation of state, but its observational prospects remain uncertain. We compare two approaches to accessing this emission: the stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB) from the BNS population and direct PM-band detections of individually resolved mergers. Using a unified inspiral--merger--post-merger (IPM) waveform prescription and the same astrophysical population model for both calculations, we evaluate representative third-generation detector configurations involving ET, CE, and a dedicated kilohertz detector. items.title: Prismatic construction of crystalline deformation rings up to p-power torsion
items.summary: We study the deformation of Galois representations which are etale realizations of finitely generated prismatic F-crystals and show the deformation functor is pro-represented by a complete Noetherian local ring whose Z_p-flat quotient coincides with Kisin's crystalline deformation ring. As a consequence, we obtain a universal prismatic F-crystal with coefficients in Kisin's crystalline deformation ring.

items.title: NS5-branes and the black hole/string transition
items.summary: Near to the onset of BTZ black hole formation in string theory is a large ensemble of 6d BPS supergravity solutions sourced by slightly separated fundamental strings and Neveu-Schwarz fivebranes. We extend the construction of these geometries to include gauge excitations of the fivebranes, and then study the energetics of D-string solitons in relation to the deconfinement transition of little strings, which are the natural non-abelian degrees of freedom that deconfine in the transition to the black hole phase.

items.title: Dark Matter Assisted Axion-Magnetic Resonance
items.summary: An oscillating axion dark matter (DM) background can enhance the conversion of another relativistic axion into photons when traversing a magnetic field. The DM background rotates photon polarization relative the magnetic orientation, which compensates the photon's and the propagating axion's dispersion relation mismatch. We relate this mechanism to Axion Magnetic Resonance (AMR) and apply it to stellar axions in the starburst galaxy M82. We analyze its enhancement to the resulting X-ray signals while accounting for the finite magnetic domain size, dark matter coherence length, DM density morphology, plasma profiles, and the detector response. items.title: Lensing ratios as a geometric probe of dark energy in the LSST and Simons Observatory era
items.summary: Ratios of galaxy-CMB and galaxy-galaxy lensing around the same foreground galaxies probe relative distances extending to recombination without a standard candle or ruler. For sufficiently narrow foreground redshift distributions, and with intrinsic alignments and lens magnification controlled, these lensing ratios (LRs) become geometrical. Here we characterize the geometrical limit and develop an end-to-end optimized framework for the probe with LSST Y10 and Simons Observatory uncertainties. In our forecast for LSST Y10, the individual ratios are measured to a median precision of 1.0%, with a total signal-to-noise ratio of 360. We then study the complementarity of LRs as an additional…

items.title: How to Play a Black Hole: Understanding Quasinormal Mode Excitation
items.summary: Understanding the excitation of black hole quasinormal modes is essential for interpreting gravitational-wave signals and inferring black hole properties from them. In this work, we investigate the excitation of the quasinormal modes of Schwarzschild black holes under controlled probes. In the absence of a source, we find that broader initial data suppresses mode excitation, enhancing the relative contribution of the late-time tail, while data localized near the light ring strongly suppresses overtones relative to the fundamental mode. On the other hand, plunging sources give rise to two distinct ringdown stages, associated with scattered radiation generated during the particle's infall…

items.title: On some off-diagonal hypergraph Ramsey problems
items.summary: We give a new short proof of a theorem of Fox and He that the $3$-uniform Ramsey number $r_3(K_4^-, K_n)$ is at least $2^{\Omega(n \log n)}$. The construction exploits a new connection with a directed graph recently introduced by Brada\v{c} in his work on off-diagonal graph Ramsey numbers. Moreover, it generalizes naturally to give sharp bounds for several extensions of this problem in higher uniformity, answering questions raised by Mubayi and Suk.

items.title: Score-Based Diffusion for Hypergraph Signals in the t-Spectral Domain
items.summary: We introduce the first score-based generative model for signals on a fixed hypergraph, formulated in the spectral domain of t-product hypergraph signal processing (t-HGSP). items.title: Contact Geometry for Generative Models: An Unbalanced Optimal Transport Formulation
items.summary: Real-world generative problems in biology, medical imaging, or robotics, rarely come with perfectly paired source and target distributions. While unbalanced Optimal Transport (uOT) provides a robust framework to bridge unpaired datasets via minimum-length paths in probability space, existing formulations based on the Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao (WFR) geometry introduce a structural bias toward high density regions, often triggering mode collapse. We introduce Contact unbalanced Optimal Transport (CuOT), a novel uOT formulation grounded in contact geometry that decouples density transport direction from mass growth to eliminate structural bias. items.title: Late-time cosmic acceleration from matter inhomogeneities: constraints from DESI DR2 and SNe Ia
items.summary: We present the first observational constraints on the Misner-Sharp (MS) mass of the universe, within a newly proposed exact General Relativity solution providing a non-perturbative description of nonlinear cosmic structure formation. At early times, when statistical homogeneity and isotropy are satisfied, our model reduces to usual FLRW cosmology, accommodating Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) data. items.title: Cantor spectrum at a fixed Diophantine frequency
items.summary: We establish that the spectrum of one-frequency analytic quasiperiodic Schrodinger operators exhibits Cantor structure in the regime of positive Lyapunov exponents for every fixed Diophantine frequency. A novel ingredient is the use of Holder continuity of the integrated density of states (IDS) to exclude energies at which eigenvalue parametrizations in finite volume have small slopes. items.title: Holographic ensembles and giant gravitons at the Leigh--Strassler fixed point
items.summary: Finite-rank observables in holographic quantum field theories provide stringent tests of string and M-theory, but remain challenging to compute when supersymmetry is non-maximal. In this paper, we study the finite rank partition function of the $\mathcal N=1$ Leigh-Strassler CFT, which admits an interacting Fermi-gas description. items.title: Baker-Akhiezer functions for Koornwinder-van Diejen integrable system
items.summary: The Koornwinder-van Diejen integrable system is a counterpart of the trigonometric Ruijsenaars integrable system (associated with the root system $A_n$) for the root system $(C_n^\vee, C_n)$. items.title: Triple-Higgs production: a window on the Higgs potential and anomalous top-Higgs couplings
items.summary: We present a comprehensive study of triple-Higgs production within the $\kappa$-framework as a probe of the Higgs potential and anomalous top-Higgs couplings. items.title: Tentative Excess Dispersion Measures toward DESI Galaxy Groups from Localized Fast Radio Bursts
items.summary: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) provide sensitive probes of ionized baryons through their dispersion measures (DMs). items.title: Modified recombination or dynamical dark energy (or both)?
items.summary: Several recent analyses report a hint of modified recombination when the latest cosmic microwave background (CMB) and baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) data are jointly analysed. items.title: Stacks of Parabolic Vector Bundles in the Geometric Langlands Program
items.summary: I define a locus inside stacks of parabolic vector bundles on smooth projective curves which is important for the construction of twisted Hecke eigensheaves in the ramified geometric Langlands program for $\mathrm{GL}_n$. I give an explicit description of this locus in the case of rank $3$ parabolic vector bundles on $\mathbb{P}^1$ with parabolic structure at four points. This example involves partial flags in the level structure as well as a non-trivial twisted equivariance condition.

items.title: CosmoMap: Predicting Hot Gas Temperature and Density from Dark Matter with a Conditioned 3D U-Net
items.summary: Mock X-ray observations of hot gas in galaxy groups, clusters and the cosmic web require its temperature and density over large volumes and many cosmologies, for which hydrodynamical simulations are expensive. items.title: How to facet a gemstone: from potential modularity to modularity lifting
items.summary: Let $F$ be a totally real field and $p\ge7$ a prime unramified in $F$. We prove that a potentially modular $p$-adic representation of $G_F$ which is potentially crystalline with distinct Hodge--Tate weights above $p$, and whose reduction is modular, non-dihedral and satisfies the usual Taylor--Wiles hypothesis, is modular. items.title: Quasifibrations in \'etale homotopy theory
items.summary: We study quasifibrations in \'etale homotopy theory and prove a criterion for a morphism of schemes to be a quasifibration in terms of its (higher) direct images for sheaves of sets and (possibly non-abelian) groups. items.title: When heavy vectors meet top partners: HVTP, a unified framework for composite Higgs searches

items.title: Zeros of the Riemann Zeta Function on the Critical Line via Bombieri and Murty-Zaharescu

The proof is based on the papers of Bombieri and Murty--Zaharescu.

items.title: $AdS$ Leading Regge Trajectory from String Field Theory
items.summary: We determine the $AdS$ mass of the leading Regge trajectory in superstring backgrounds $AdS_5\times S^5$, $AdS_4\times\mathbb{CP}^3$, and $AdS_3\times S^3\times{\cal M}_4$ with pure Ramond-Ramond (RR) flux for both ${\cal M}_4=S^3\times S^1$ and ${\cal M}_4=T^4$, to the second order in the expansion with respect to the background RR flux by solving the linearized equations of motion in closed superstring field theory. items.title: Thermodynamic constraints on warm inflation with the Standard Model

items.title: Toward Solving the Galactic Foreground Problem in Gravitational-Wave Astronomy with Machine Learning

items.title: Enhanced spatial resolution and performance for N-body simulation of self-interacting dark matter

items.title: Holographic Entanglement Entropy of Network CFT

items.title: Wave interactions for the two-dimensional self-similar Euler equations of nonconvex gases

items.title: Global Existence and Large-Time Behavior of Strong Solutions to the Two-Dimensional Full Compressible Navier-Stokes Equations with Degenerate Heat Conductivity and Large Initial Data
items.summary: In this paper, we investigate the two-dimensional full compressible Navier--Stokes system with degenerate heat conductivity in three settings: the periodic domain, a general bounded simply connected domain subject to Navier-slip boundary conditions, and the whole space with non-vacuum far-field density. items.title: Supercuspidal representations and types via double covers and the Fourier--Weil representation
items.summary: We present a construction of supercuspidal representations and types for tame $p$-adic groups whose input is a generic essentially depth-zero representation of a double covers of twisted Levi subgroups. This clarifies and simplifies existing constructions by automatically producing and explaining the twisting quadratic character of Fintzen--Kaletha--Spice, the roots of unity in the Harish-Chandra character formula, and making the connection to the Galois side of the local Langlands correspondence immediate. The main innovation is the use of a Fourier model of the Weil representation defined on an extension of the symplectic group by the Witt group.

items.title: Quaternionic geometry of symplectic and contact pairs
items.summary: We introduce quaternionic analogues of symplectic pairs, contact--symplectic pairs and contact pairs. A hyper symplectic pair consists of three symplectic pairs whose sums form a positive quaternionic triple, while the contact analogues are defined through single or double symplectization. We prove that radial invariance of the induced complex structures is equivalent to the coincidence of the characteristic distributions, yielding a local product decomposition. Under a natural normalization, hyper contact--symplectic pairs are locally products of a $3$-Sasakian and a hyper-K\"ahler manifold and induce canonical $3$-quasi-Sasakian structures, whereas hyper contact pairs are locally…

items.title: Multi-Component Axion Dark Matter Revisited and the Role of Ultralight ALPs
items.summary: In this work, we revisit the multi-component axion dark matter (DM) scenario and explore the role of ultralight axion-like particles (ALPs). After briefly reviewing maximal axion mixing, we incorporate a stochastic axion mixing mechanism that generalizes it by relaxing the requirement of a uniform hierarchy among the axion decay constants. We find that, depending on the parameters, either the QCD axion or an ALP can dominate the DM abundance after mixing; once axion mass contributions are included, the heaviest ALPs tend to prevail. In a two-component framework, stochastic mixing significantly enlarges the allowed parameter space for the QCD axion decay constant, enabling the QCD axion to…

items.summary: We study fractional triangle decompositions of two-dimensional simplicial complexes, unifying the settings of Nash-Williams' conjecture on triangle decompositions and the high-dimensional Dirac problem for Steiner triple systems. We prove that every sufficiently large two-dimensional simplicial complex with minimum degree at least $(1-d_1)n$ and maximum missing codegree at most $d_2n$ admits a fractional triangle decomposition, provided $d_1/0.21+d_2/0.27\leq 1$. items.title: Monsky's nodal cubic and the arithmetic of Frobenius invariants
items.summary: We prove Monsky's conjecture on the colengths of the ideals $(x^q,y^q,z^q,h^j)$ in $\mathbb{F}_2[x,y,z]$, where $h=x^3+y^3+xyz$, $q=2^e$, and $0\le j\le q$. We derive Monsky's recursion by interchanging the values of sections of syzygy bundles on the two branches at the node of the cubic $h=0$. For the hypersurface $uv+h=0$, the Hilbert-Kunz and Frobenius splitting series are algebraic of degree two over $\mathbb{Q}(w)$. For $uv+h(X_1)+\cdots+h(X_m)=0$, where the $X_i$ are disjoint triples of variables and $m\ge 2$, both series are transcendental over $\mathbb{Q}(w)$. When $m=2$, we express the Hilbert-Kunz multiplicity in terms of a period of an elliptic curve in characteristic zero. This…

items.title: On derived Galois deformation rings in characteristic 0 and a conjecture of Venkatesh
items.summary: Let $\Pi$ be a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of $\operatorname{GL}_n$ over a CM field $F$, and $\rho$ its associated Galois representation in characteristic 0. With mild assumptions, we use the Taylor--Wiles method to define a free action of the potentially semistable derived deformation ring of $\rho$ on the $\Pi$-part of the $p$-adic cohomology of $\operatorname{GL}_n/F$, confirming a prediction of Venkatesh. As a key step, we establish an equivalence between the derived deformation ring of $\rho$ with the completion at the point corresponding to $\rho$ of the derived deformation ring of the mod $p$ reduction $\bar{\rho}$, generalising well-known results by Kisin.

items.title: The generalized Franchetta conjecture for some hyper-K\"ahler varieties, III
items.summary: The generalized Franchetta conjecture states that for a locally complete family of polarized hyper-K\"ahler varieties, the generically defined cycles on any fiber of the universal family over the moduli stack inject into cohomology via the cycle class map. We prove the generalized Franchetta conjecture for the family of double EPW sextics discovered by O'Grady and for the family of double EPW cubes discovered by Iliev-Kapustka-Kapustka-Ranestad. We also prove a Franchetta-type result for the relative square of the universal family of double EPW sextics, which allows to relate double EPW sextics and Gushel-Mukai fourfolds on the level of motives. The proof involves the geometry of…

items.title: Hodge cycles of Klein hypersurfaces
items.summary: We study the space of Hodge cycles on Klein varieties. Relating it to the Hodge characters in a covering Fermat variety, we decompose the space of Hodge characters into a part generated by classes of rational subvarieties, and a non-trivial part which we call exceptional. Using Dirichlet characters we show that the exceptional part is always finite. Furthermore, we give sufficient conditions under which there are no exceptional characters, providing infinitely many new cases of the Hodge conjecture for Klein varieties. Finally, we describe the set of exceptional characters of Klein varieties for small dimensions.

items.title: Combinatorial relative orientability for toric and tropical geometry
items.summary: Many problems in enumerative geometry are solved by computing the degree of the top Chern class of a suitable vector bundle. Results from $\mathbb{A}^1$-homotopy theory allow to answer enumerative questions over arbitrary fields, replacing the top Chern class by the Euler class in Chow-Witt groups. For its degree to be well-defined, one needs the vector bundle to be relatively oriented. Another way to solve enumerative problems is to translate them to tropical geometry, where they become combinatorial problems. In this paper, we give a combinatorial description of relative orientability for vector bundles over smooth proper toric varieties. We show that it behaves well under…

items.title: Extremal Projectors and the Virasoro Algebra
items.summary: Extremal projectors are universal operators projecting onto the highest weight space in a representation. Their existence and uniqueness (as formal series) are known for a broad range of Lie superalgebras and quantum groups. We consider a class of Lie superalgebras that contains reductive finite-dimensional Lie algebras as well as the Virasoro algebra. We prove the existence and uniqueness of an extremal projector for this class. The existence proof is given in terms of a recursive algorithm which can be used to compute the coefficients. To illustrate the method, we compute the terms for the Virasoro extremal projector up to order 6. Furthermore, we formulate a conjecture for the…

items.summary: We study the geometric connection between a stretched grand-unified state, proton decay, and electroweak Kaluza--Klein (KK) resonances in a dark-dimension-inspired interval model. The gravitational length sets the five-dimensional Planck scale, while a shorter gauge interval controls the KK spectrum and the stretched-state mass. We construct normalized fermion and Higgs profiles, diagonalize the neutral-vector sector, and determine its fermionic widths. Proton partial lifetimes are evaluated using a two-operator, SU(5)-inspired effective matching prescription. items.title: Feynman integrals, coactions and Lie-algebra representations
items.summary: We outline a link between canonical differential equations of Feynman integrals and matrix representations of flat connections taking values in certain Lie algebras. Leveraging insights from string theory and properties of periods associated with these Lie algebras, we deduce single-valued solutions to the differential equations and coactions for the integrals. We introduce a novel form of the differential equations which connects with the representation theory of the Lie algebras and may depart from $\varepsilon$-factorisation in a controlled way. We illustrate the formalism through relevant examples.

items.title: Brane Tilings and Polygons with Two Interior Points
items.summary: We fully classify the brane tilings and the 4d N=1 supersymmetric quiver gauge theories corresponding to toric Calabi-Yau 3-folds whose toric diagrams are convex lattice polygons with two interior lattice points. There are 45 such polygons up to GL(2,Z) transformations and lattice translations: 5 triangles, 19 quadrilaterals, 16 pentagons and 5 hexagons. We identify all 323 toric phases corresponding to these toric Calabi-Yau 3-folds. For every toric phase, we present the brane tiling with its quiver and superpotential, the perfect matching matrix and the F- and D-term charge matrices. items.title: A covariant analysis of massless Dirac fields in LRS spacetimes
items.summary: We investigate the massless Dirac field in locally rotationally symmetric (LRS) spacetimes using a covariant spinorial-fluid representation, with the spinor current and spin direction aligned with the LRS frame. When the current has both vorticity and sheet twist, characterized by a constant ratio $\lambda$, the LRS integrability condition relates evolution and propagation derivatives, reducing the field equations to an ordinary differential system that can be integrated exactly. The integrability of the chiral angle forces the heat flux to vanish and the source to saturate the null energy condition along the two radial null directions. items.title: BMS Charges from Null Hypersurfaces
items.summary: We show how the gravitational dynamics, phase space and Noether charges of the BMS group at future null infinity $\mathscr{I}^+$ can be derived as limits of their analogues on null hypersurfaces at finite distance. The Bondi mass-loss and angular-momentum evolution equations arise as limits of the Raychaudhuri and Damour constraints. The Ashtekar--Streubel (aka Wald--Zoupas) symplectic potential arises as a specific member of a two-parameter family of null-boundary symplectic potentials, corresponding to the Dirichlet (aka canonical) polarization, while the other members differ by field-space exact terms, leading to the same radiative pre-symplectic structure but potentially different BMS…

items.title: Projectivized ASEP-Bethe system and counting solutions
items.summary: This paper addresses the problem of counting solutions to the ASEP-Bethe ansatz equations. In an earlier preprint, Brattain, Do, and Saenz presented an algebro-geometric method for counting the number of such solutions. As their method relies on sophisticated machinery, it requires advanced knowledge of algebraic geometry and topology. In this paper, we provide an alternative and simpler method for counting solutions, based on a standard intersection theory on projective varieties. We take a conventional approach in algebraic geometry: ``Projectivize the problem and count degrees.'' We introduce a projectivized version of the ASEP-Bethe equations, whose solution set is realized as a…

items.title: Nonlinear stability of periodic waves in the Benjamin-Ono equation
items.summary: We construct the Lyapunov functional for the periodic waves of the Benjamin-Ono equation based on the conservation of momentum, energy, and a higher-order energy, which exists due to integrability. Positivity of the second variation of the Lyapunov functional for perturbations in Sobolev space $H^1(\mathbb{R})$ is established by utilizing the basis properties of eigenfunctions of the linearized Benjamin-Ono equation in $L^2(\mathbb{R})$. Coercivity of the Lyapunov functional for co-periodic and multiple-periodic perturbations yields the nonlinear orbital stability of the periodic waves in the periodic domain.

items.title: The Markov Property on Decorated Metric Planar Maps
items.summary: We introduce decorated metric planar maps: planar maps whose edges $e$ are replaced by segments $[0,w_e]$, together with a continuous function on the resulting metric space, the decoration. items.title: Constraining Regular Black Hole Models with the Effective Field Theory treatment of General Relativity
items.summary: In this paper, we present a method for using perturbative predictions from treating general relativity as an effective field theory to constrain non-perturbative approaches to quantum gravity in black hole contexts. We start by reviewing a known result from this framework, which estimates the first quantum corrections to the interaction energy of a static particle near a black hole. We then propose a way to test non-perturbative quantum black hole models - specifically those formulated as modified Schwarzschild metrics, also known as regular black holes - against this perturbative result. items.title: Revealing Dark Matter in the Dark-Electron Rate of Xenon Detectors
items.summary: There is high interest in improving experimental sensitivity to sub-GeV dark matter (DM) that scatters with electrons, as compelling theoretical models seem within reach. At the lowest DM masses, most of the expected signal lies in the single-electron regime, but so do large backgrounds. Xenon experiments therefore either do not yet search there at all or, as in XENONnT, apply cuts so severe that only $\sim$$10^{-4}$ of the exposure is retained, with sensitivity set by the criterion $S \lesssim B$, where those are the signal and background counts. items.title: Scale-dependent Dark Matter in a Multi-component Cosmological Framework: Distinct Components Governing Galactic and Cosmological Dynamics
items.summary: In this work we generalize the concept of scale-dependent equation of state dark matter from galactic to cosmological scales. At galactic scales, the scale-dependent equation of state which successfully describes dark matter dominated galaxies has a nearly isothermal equation of state of the form $P(r)=K(r)\rho(r)$, where the entropy function $K(r)$ is radius dependent and slowly varying with the galactic radius. items.title: Superheavy gravitational dark matter from runaway bubble collisions
items.summary: A stable particle that couples only through gravity is pair-produced in collisions of runaway bubble walls by graviton exchange. For a transition of duration $1/\beta$, a Dirac fermion reaches the yield $Y_X\simeq6.8\times10^{-3}(H/\beta)(T_{\rm reh}/M_{\rm P})^3$, where $H$ is the Hubble rate of the vacuum energy, $T_{\rm reh}$ the reheating temperature and $M_{\rm P}$ the reduced Planck mass. The yield is flat up to masses near $(H/\beta)M_{\rm P}/\nu^2$, where $\nu$ of order one sets the wall-field excursion. Gravity alone then gives dark matter up to about $10^{17}$~GeV at reheating temperatures far below its mass, where freeze-in fails.

items.title: Modularity of Heegner Cycles and Arithmetic Inner Products on Kuga-Sato Varieties

items.title: Leray's Problem for the Stationary Navier-Stokes Equations with Low-Regularity Data in Planar and Three-Dimensional Axisymmetric Lipschitz Domains
items.summary: In this paper, we study the steady Navier-Stokes Dirichlet problem in bounded planar and three-dimensional axisymmetric domains with finitely many disjoint Lipschitz boundary components. Individual component fluxes are subject to no smallness or sign restrictions. In three dimensions the domain and data are axisymmetric, and swirl is allowed. items.title: Note on polychromatic coloring of hereditary hypergraph families III
items.summary: For every integer $h\ge4$ we construct a hereditary family of hypergraphs with $m_2=h$ and \[ m_3\ge 2(h-1)+2\left\lfloor\frac{h-1}{3}\right\rfloor+1 \approx \frac{8}{3}m_2. \] This improves the lower bound $m_3\ge 2m_2$ from the preceding notes for every $m_2\ge4$. We also show that the worst-case integrality gap of the weighted transversal problem over hereditary families with $m_2\le h$ is between $h-1$ and $5000h$. items.title: On the measure of Neighborhoods of Kakeya and Truncated Nikodym Sets
items.summary: We show that there exist Kakeya sets in $\mathbb{R}^d$ whose $\delta$-neighborhoods have measure $\lesssim |\log\delta|^{-(d-1)}$. We also show that the measure of a $\delta$-neighborhood of an $\epsilon$-truncated Nikodym set in $\mathbb{R}^2$ $\gtrsim \epsilon^{-1}|\log\delta|^{-1}$, for $\delta$ small enough. The sufficiently small scale depends on the Nikodym set and on $\epsilon$.

items.title: TPTL-dist: A Formalised Calculus with Proof Automation for Verifying Real-Time Distributed Systems
items.summary: We introduce TPTL-dist, a temporal logic and labelled sequent calculus for specifying and verifying real-time distributed systems. TPTL-dist is formalised in Agda to provide machine-checked correctness and tool support, including automation through a proof search that runs inside Agda. The logic extends Timed Propositional Temporal Logic (TPTL) with past operators, freeze quantification, comparisons between time expressions, domain-specific atoms, and an induction principle on time. We provide a world-based semantics, develop an interval-annotated calculus, and establish its soundness w.r.t. the semantics. items.title: The chiral $M^{3,2}$ theory: partition functions beyond large-$N$ and quantum holography
items.summary: We identify families of Bethe vacua in the chiral $M^{3,2}$ theory whose individual free energies grow as $N^{3/2}$. At a distinguished mixed Chern--Simons coupling, the baryonic magnetic flux distinguishes members of this family of vacua. We also study the three-sphere partition function numerically in the 't Hooft limit and Cardy limit, and propose an all-order Airy formula. The four-derivative and one-loop corrections are precision tests of holography.

In analogy to pulsar timing, we develop a correlation statistic between pairs of stellar deflections for astrometry to search for a stochastic GW background. items.title: IADR: Interface-Augmented Neural Operator for Phase-Field Mean-Curvature Flow
items.summary: The Allen-Cahn equation is one of the standard phase-field models for mean-curvature flow (MCF), parameterised by the diffuse-interface width $\varepsilon$. Practical simulations span a range of $\varepsilon$, so a single model covering this range is needed. PDE-specific neural operators are accurate but must be retrained at every $\varepsilon$; general neural operators cover $\varepsilon$ in one model but lose the phase-field structure of the target. items.title: A symplectic Hilbert hotel
items.summary: We construct a smooth global symplectomorphism of an infinite dimensional separable Hilbert space mapping a ball of large radius to a subset of a cylinder of small radius. This symplectomorphism and its inverse map bounded sets to bounded sets. This example shows that Gromov's non-squeezing theorem does not generalize to infinite dimensional Hilbert spaces without further assumptions.

items.title: A $(17/7-o(1))n$ Circuit Lower Bound for Binary-Encoded 3-SAT
items.summary: We strengthen the elementary $n-1$ circuit lower bound for a specified binary encoding of 3-SAT to $(17/7)n-O(n\log\log n/\log n)$ gates over the full two-input Boolean basis, with unrestricted depth and sharing. We provide Lean proofs of the finite inequality and the asymptotic bound for arbitrary acyclic binary circuits.

items.title: Equivariant Localization for $K(n)$-Local Gromov-Witten Invariants with Applications to Gopakumar-Vafa Invariants
items.summary: For certain complex-oriented $K(n)$-local cohomology theories, we establish equivariant localization formulas for global Kuranishi charts and a Riemann-Roch formula. items.title: Flavor-resolved screening length of a moving quarkonium in a lattice-calibrated holographic QCD plasma

items.title: Vector boson scattering in composite Higgs models
items.summary: Vector boson scattering is a powerful tool to test the mechanism of electroweak symmetry breaking. We focus on Composite Higgs models with an underlying fermionic description and assume that only one pseudo Nambu-Goldstone boson contributes to electroweak symmetry breaking, which we identify as the Higgs state of the Standard Model. In these scenarios, LHC data imply lower bounds on the predicted resonances below 2 TeV depending on the scenario. Using $WZjj$ production as a benchmark, we demonstrate that the tails of various distributions nevertheless show significant deviations from Standard Model predictions. This holds in particular for the case of longitudinally polarised vector bosons.

items.title: A complete knot invariant from grid diagrams
items.summary: Using grid diagrams, we define an infinite graph associated to each knot type. We prove that the isomorphism class of this grid graph is a complete invariant of the knot, up to mirroring. Even more, we prove that algorithmically determinable finite parts of this graph are enough to determine the knot type.

items.title: Low-Rank Tensor Representations for Efficient Multimarginal Optimal Transport

This structure enables efficient algorithms with a low memory footprint. We establish approximation bounds for the resulting low-rank formulations and demonstrate experimentally that the proposed algorithms substantially reduce computational time while achieving solutions with low transport cost.

Addressing questions of Buff--Epstein--Koch, we construct a sequence of real, bitransitive centres in the critical orbit relation curve $C_2$ which degenerates in moduli space, and whose Lyapunov exponents tend to infinity whilst the Thurston eigenvalues satisfy $\frac{1}{10}< |\lambda|<1$. We also show the Thurston eigenvalues across all bitransitive centres in $C_2$ have a spectral gap on compact subsets of the curve.

items.title: Is Gravitational-Wave Waveform Systematics a Bottleneck for Formation Channel Inferences using Effective-Spin and Mass-Ratio?
items.summary: Gravitational-wave measurements of the effective spin $\chi_\text{eff}$ and mass ratio $q$ help distinguish binary black hole formation channels, motivating a search for structure in the $\chi_\text{eff} - q$ plane. However, both these quantities are known to be strongly correlated in GW parameter estimation since both enter the leading-order spin-orbit term together, and thus, the detectors cannot easily tell them apart. In this work, we harness the susceptibility of such measurements to waveform systematics by using injection-recovery studies with NRSur7dq4 as the true signal and SEOBNRv5PHM and IMRPhenomTPHM for parameter inferences. Our study shows that, though there can be some…

items.title: Probe branes from equivariant volumes
items.summary: Classical Euclidean probe actions control non-perturbative weights and extended observables in holography. We present a geometric prescription for M2-branes in arbitrary BPS backgrounds and D3-branes in the five-form sector of type IIB. The framework accommodates compact and non-compact supersymmetric worldvolumes in both internal and spacetime directions, expressing their actions as relative equivariant pairings. Under stated extension and boundary assumptions, equivariant volumes evaluate these pairings without explicit background metrics and provide a regularization for non-compact probes. Examples in $\mathrm{AdS}_4\times SE_7$ backgrounds dual to ABJM, ADHM and flavored quiver…

items.title: PINN-Slicer: Exploiting Rotational Symmetry to Solve the Photon Orbit Equation Around a Black Hole
items.summary: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) typically struggle with long-horizon domains, often requiring the network to be retrained as the domain grows. We present PINN-Slicer, a method for second-order autonomous ordinary differential equations, $\ddot{u} = G(u, \dot{u})$, which exploits the invariance of this class of equations under translations of the independent variable. A single PINN, embedded within a solution ansatz that enforces the initial conditions explicitly, is trained on a thin slice of the independent variable using Sobol-sampled initial conditions. The PINN is then deployed recursively, slice-by-slice, across the full domain. We demonstrate PINN-Slicer on the nonlinear…

items.title: On generalized linear periods for inner forms of GLn
items.summary: Let $\mathrm{D}$ be a central division algebra of index $e$ over a non-Archimedean local field $\mathrm{F}$ of characteristic zero. For every integer $n\ge 1$ and every $s\in \mathbb{R}$, we classify the irreducible smooth representations of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathrm{D})$ that admit a nonzero linear form transforming under the subgroup $\mathrm{GL}_1(\mathrm{D})\times\mathrm{GL}_{n-1}(\mathrm{D})$ by the character $\nu^{es}\otimes\nu^{-es}$. We further show that such a linear form is unique up to scalars, and we characterize its existence in terms of Langlands parameters.

items.title: RMT${}_2$: Random Spectral Correlations for CFT${}_2$ and AdS${}_3$ Gravity
items.summary: We present the full framework of RMT${}_2$, a consistent unification of random matrix theory and modular invariance. The systematic prescription, which augments the existing construction by incorporating spin, lifts random matrix correlators to $\text{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ Poincar\'e sums of their Mellin transforms, in a manner which enforces random matrix correlations near extremality in every spinning primary sector. The resulting RMT${}_2$ correlators are further expressible in terms of an orthogonal basis of Eisenstein series and Maass cusp forms. We demonstrate the construction by lifting the two-point correlators at arbitrary genus of the Airy model, in both unitary and orthogonal…

items.title: Probing the CKM Origin of CP Violation with Paramagnetic EDMs and Rare Kaon Decays
items.summary: In the Standard Model, paramagnetic electric dipole moments (EDMs) are dominated by kaon exchange, which pairs the CP-violating short-distance transition $s\to d\,e^+e^-$ with a CP-conserving weak kaon-nucleon coupling. Long-distance two-photon exchange, which dominates $K_L\to e^+e^-$, gives an electron vertex about thirty-five times larger than the short-distance one and could obscure this origin. We show that it does not: the two-photon vertex conserves CP and must be paired with the CP-violating penguin component of the nucleon coupling, whose relative size is $3\times10^{-4}$, so that electromagnetic corrections stay at the few-percent level. Paramagnetic EDMs therefore measure…

items.title: The type-D accelerating Taub-NUT spacetime: construction, geometry and physical properties
items.summary: We investigate the geometry and physical properties of the vacuum type-D accelerating Taub--NUT spacetime in the sector with vanishing Kerr rotation. We recover its normalized metric from the Pleba\'nski--Demia\'nski family and a dressed finite binary, tracking the horizon Killing directions through the large-companion limit. The black-hole and acceleration horizons have distinct projective Killing generators, and their intrinsic horizon geometry yields a relation between polar Gaussian curvatures and cone angles that differs from that of the type-I accelerating Taub--NUT solution without requiring a matching of acceleration parameters. We establish separability of the type-D null…

items.title: Height function covariance and point-to-line coalescence in the directed landscape
items.summary: We prove an integration-by-parts formula for the KPZ fixed point with a deterministic $C_b^1$ terminal reward. For flat data, let $C(x)$ denote the spatial height covariance at time one. For almost every $x>0$, we show that $-C'(x)$ is the probability that the point-to-line geodesics started at $0$ and $x$ coalesce by time one. The proof uses Gaussian integration by parts for the O'Connell--Yor polymer, followed by the zero-temperature and directed-landscape limits.

items.title: Lighting up LZ with Loopy Transitions in a leptophilic Dark Sector
items.summary: We study the direct detection phenomenology and cosmology of a multicomponent dark sector with a leptophilic t-channel portal. The coupling to right-handed Standard Model leptons is mediated by a charged vector-like fermion, allowing both a scalar and a vector dark candidate to connect to the SM through the same mediator. Motivated by the high-energy nuclear-recoil event recently reported by the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment, we consider a nearly degenerate dark sector with mass splittings of order a few hundred keV and investigate the resulting inelastic transitions. Concretely, we focus on endothermic scattering of the dark states, which can shift the recoil spectrum towards the high-energy…

items.title: Error estimates for a structure-preserving finite-element scheme of quasi-incompressible Navier-Stokes-Maxwell-Stefan systems
items.summary: A conforming finite-element scheme for quasi-incompressible Navier-Stokes-Maxwell-Stefan systems in a bounded domain with periodic boundary conditions is presented. The system consists of the Navier-Stokes equations, together with a quasi-incompressibility constraint, coupled with the cross-diffusion Maxwell--Stefan equations. The numerical scheme preserves the partial masses and the quasi-incompressibility constraint and dissipates the discrete energy. First-order error estimates in space and time are shown for a diffusion-augmented mobility matrix by using the relative energy method and suitable projection error estimates. Numerical experiments in two space dimensions illustrate the…

items.title: A consequence of the classical Lindel\"of Hypothesis for the density of zeros of general Dirichlet series
items.summary: Supposing the Lindel\"of Hypothesis for the Riemann zeta function we prove that the density hypothesis holds for Res>3/4 for a large class of Dirichlet series. The first result of similar type was reached by G\'abor Hal\'asz and Paul Tur\'an in 1969.

items.title: Constraining Intergalactic Dust with Supernova Color Evolution: Current Constraints from DES and Forecasts for LSST and Roman
items.summary: Dust is an important systematic in precision Type Ia supernova (SN Ia) cosmology, and while dust in the Milky Way and SN host galaxies has been extensively studied, the impact of potential intergalactic dust is less well constrained. Using estimates from B. M\'enard et al. (2010), we find that current intergalactic dust bounds could shift SN distance moduli by up to 0.02 mag at $z \gtrsim 1$ from simulations. However, we show dust models can be constrained independently by SN samples themselves via a specific predicted redshift-dependent evolution observed in SN colors. While current data from the Dark Energy Survey (DES) cannot distinguish between various amounts of intergalactic dust in…

items.title: Halo spin-axis correlations in IllustrisTNG: Lagrangian-to-Eulerian separation mapping, baryonic effects, and redshift-space distortions
items.summary: We investigate correlations of halo and stellar spin axes in the TNG300 volume of the IllustrisTNG simulations and compare them with a model based on linear tidal torque theory (LTTT). Dark matter (DM) halo spin axes at $z = 0$ exhibit positive correlations as a function of Lagrangian pair separation. The LTTT-based model describes their separation dependence well, with weak variation in the fitted amplitude across mass thresholds. A Lagrangian-to-Eulerian separation mapping based on the conditional distributions of initial separations at fixed present-day separation, measured directly from the simulations, allows the model to reproduce the overall trends in both real and redshift space…

items.title: On the level lines of bilayer potentials with a finite number of harmonics
items.summary: We consider ``bilayer'' potentials formed by the superposition of two periodic potentials in a plane. We assume that both potentials share the same rotational symmetry and employ an approximation involving a finite number of harmonics in their Fourier expansions. An analysis of the level lines of the resulting quasiperiodic potential (a problem posed by S.P. Novikov) near the percolation threshold makes it possible to describe the behavior of large-scale closed level lines in this limit. The results presented here can also be applied to broader classes of bilayer potentials that possess ``good'' analytical properties.

items.title: Hamiltonian approach to isospectrality in nonrotating black holes
items.summary: In this work, we revisit the isospectrality of black hole perturbations from a Hamiltonian perspective. For a nonrotating, uncharged system, we present a convenient canonical description of the background degrees of freedom that facilitates comparison with the usual Lagrangian formulation. This allows us to identify phase-space counterparts of the superpotential and the algebraically special modes and show that they satisfy the expected isospectral relations, at least on shell or off shell modulo some subtle lapse redefinitions. Finally, we investigate the extent to which these results persist in theories that effectively modify general relativity. In this setting, we formally quantify the…

items.title: The irreducibility of tame character varieties
items.summary: Tame character varieties are known to be irreducible when the parametrised local systems have monodromies lying in closures of generic conjugacy classes; we will establish their irreducibility without the genericity assumption. A combination of nonabelian Hodge correspondence and variation of parabolic weights reduces the problem to the case of almost generic semi-simple monodromies, which is then treated using a point-counting result of Scognamiglio for nongeneric character stacks. The connectedness result is then used to clarify a couple of facts concerning the symplectic leaves.

items.title: Frobenius lifts on invariant subrings, with applications to rational double points and perfectoid towers
items.summary: We study Frobenius lifts on invariant subrings and give applications to rational double points and perfectoid towers. We realize rational double points of ADE over $W(k)$ as invariant subrings $A^G$, where $A$ is a ramified two-dimensional complete regular local ring and $G$ is a finite linearly reductive subgroup scheme of $\mathrm{SL}_{2,W(k)}$. We also prove a general theorem on the existence of Frobenius lifts on invariant subrings: if a flat affine group scheme $G$ over $W(k)$ admits a functorial Reynolds operator and a relative Frobenius lift, then any formal power series ring equipped with a linear action of $G$ admits a Frobenius lift that restricts to a Frobenius lift on the…

items.title: Testing the Unitarity of Three-Flavor Neutrino Mixing above the GUT Scale
items.summary: We investigate how physics between the grand-unification and Planck scales affects neutrino mixing in the standard three-flavor framework, distinguishing genuine non unitarity from unitary shifts of the mixing parameters. First, we show that heavy gauge singlet states at or above the grand-unification scale induce deviations from unitarity of the effective (3\times3) Pontecorvo Maki Nakagawa Sakata (PMNS) matrix, suppressed by the ratio of the light-neutrino mass to the heavy mass. The resulting effects are estimated to be of order (10^{-27}), far below current oscillation constraints. Second, we examine the impact of a flavor-blind dimension-five Weinberg operator suppressed by a…

items.title: An Electromagnetic Ergoregion Limits the Reconnection-Driven Penrose Process
items.summary: Magnetic reconnection taps black-hole rotational energy via negative-energy ejecta, but field geometry itself can forbid such ejection inside the spacetime ergoregion. We identify a covariant electromagnetic (EM) ergoregion for general degenerate, magnetically dominated fields in stationary spacetimes. Outside the EM ergoregion, even ultrarelativistic field-guided ejecta cannot attain negative Killing energy. For Alfv\'enic reconnection outflows, the magnetization threshold scales inversely with the transverse distance to the EM ergosurface. The mass-loaded Kerr model places the EM ergosurface at about 75% of the radial interval from the horizon to the spacetime ergosurface, close to the…

items.title: A Genetic Algorithm Approach to Reconstructing Scalar-Tensor Lagrangians
items.summary: Recent DESI baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) data, combined with cosmic microwave background (CMB) and Type Ia supernovae observations, have been interpreted as evidence for dynamical dark energy whose equation of state crosses the phantom divide $w=-1$. Such a crossing cannot be realized smoothly by a minimally coupled scalar field $\varphi$, but can arise naturally in scalar-tensor theories. We present a data-driven framework that reconstructs the scalar-tensor Lagrangian directly from observations, using a genetic algorithm to evolve the symbolic expressions for the nonminimal coupling $F(\varphi)$ and the scalar potential $U(\varphi)$. Each candidate is evaluated through a forward…

items.title: Integrable nearest neighbor interaction Hamiltonians and the rigidity of the Toda Lattice
items.summary: We consider mechanical Hamiltonian systems, where the potentials describe a nearest-neighbor interaction law. In this setting, a non trivial example of an integrable system is the celebrated Toda lattice. We study deformations of this potential (for three particles), and show that some classes of analytic deformations of the potential break its integrability, without assuming anything about the form of the integrals. This result is reminiscent of local rigidity of ellipses in billiards. The proof relies on the fact that high energy orbits for the Toda lattice approximate billiard orbits in some polytopes.

items.title: Environmental resonances in extreme-mass-ratio inspirals within boson clouds
items.summary: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) offer a promising probe of matter environments around massive black holes through gravitational-wave (GW) observations. We investigate orbital resonances induced by conservative gravitational perturbations from such environments. Combining a multiparameter expansion with the action-angle formalism, we derive a general resonance condition for generic bound Kerr orbits. Applying this framework to ultralight scalar clouds formed through black hole superradiance, we show that orbital resonances can arise from a single-mode cloud without requiring transitions between cloud modes. Our analysis demonstrates that these resonances can lead to significant GW…

items.title: Origin of flavour cancellations in thermal leptogenesis
items.summary: In thermal leptogenesis with three hierarchical heavy neutrinos $N_1$, $N_2$ and $N_3$, the baryon asymmetry can be the small remainder of large contributions that cancel. Interference terms in the CP asymmetry are known to contribute to the final asymmetry through flavour-dependent washout. However, it remains unclear where the cancellation occurs, how large the interference contribution is, and how the accuracy of approximate equations changes when this information is lost. We split the CP asymmetry into diagonal and off-diagonal parts in the charged-lepton basis and evolve them with Standard Model transport equations. We find that the cancellation occurs mainly between the diagonal and…

items.title: R\'enyi multi-entropy from Riemann surfaces
items.summary: We compute vacuum tripartite R\'enyi multi-entropy in a two-dimensional compact-boson conformal field theory (CFT). For every integer R\'enyi index $n\geq2$, we evaluate the partition function on the replica Riemann surface for disjoint intervals, obtaining the twist four-point function in terms of a ratio of theta functions. An independent calculation of the partition function on a Fermat curve yields the adjacent three-point coefficient. In the fusion limit, the Riemann surface for disjoint intervals degenerates into two Fermat curves, and the residue of the four-point function reproduces the squared three-point coefficient, as required by the operator product expansion. The genuine…

items.title: Critical exponent for Nakao's problem in three space dimensions
items.summary: We study a system consisting of a semilinear damped wave equation coupled to a semilinear wave equation in three space dimensions. We determine the sharp condition on the exponents of nonlinear terms that separates global existence for sufficiently small initial data from finite-time blow-up even for arbitrarily small data satisfying suitable positivity assumptions. To prove global existence, we combine a weighted pointwise estimate for the damped wave equation, which we established in earlier work, with a new one for the wave equation. The new pointwise estimate for the wave equation uses a combination of a parabolic weight and a light-cone weight. For the proof of blow-up, pointwise…

items.title: From nested soft-collinear subtraction to NNLO QCD predictions with large language models
items.summary: We investigate whether large language models can construct reliable and efficient codes for computing NNLO QCD corrections to collider processes, starting from the general formula derived within the nested soft-collinear subtraction scheme. We use Higgs production in weak-boson fusion with and without an additional jet to compare numerical implementations by large language models, subject to various degrees of supervision, against a human-written reference code.

items.title: Pairing Powers of Pythagorean Pairs II
items.summary: Let $(a,b,c)$ be a pythagorean triple, i.e., $a^2+b^2=c^2$. Then $(c,a)$ and $(c,b)$ are hypotenuse-leg pairs (hl-pairs), i.e., pairs $(c,d)$ of positive integers such that $c^2-d^2$ is a non-zero square. An hl-pair $(c,d)$ is called a pythapotent hl-pair of degree $h$ if there is a pythagorean pair $(k,l)$, which is not a multiple of the pythagorean pair $(d,\sqrt{c^2-d^2})$, such that $(c^hk,d^hl)$ is again an hl-pair. To each hl-pair $(c,d)$ and each $h\geq 1$ we assign the elliptic curve $\Gamma_{c^h,d^h}: y^2=x^3+(c^{2h}-d^{2h})x^2-c^{2h}d^{2h}x$ and show that its torsion group is $\Bbb Z/2\Bbb Z\times\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$ and that $(c,d)$ is a pythapotent hl-pair of degree $h$ if and…

items.title: Screening of New Abelian Long-Range Forces
items.summary: We study how bounds on new $U(1)$ long-range forces, resulting from gauging the Standard Model symmetries $B-L$ and $L_a-L_b$, $a,b=e,\mu,\tau$, are modified if the mediator mass is generated by the Higgs mechanism. Large baryonic and leptonic charges of astronomical bodies displace the Higgs field from its vacuum value, resulting in charge screening. Depending on the $U(1)$ Higgs mass, the screening relaxes the bounds on the new force strength and mediator mass from equivalence principle violation and neutrino oscillations experiments, and eliminates the bounds on the muonic $L_\mu-L_\tau$ force from neutron star binaries.

items.title: Global well-posedness for the focusing Gross-Pitaevskii equation in the one-dimensional Zhidkov space
items.summary: We show global well-posedness for the focusing Gross-Pitaevskii equation in one spatial dimension, with initial data in the Zhidkov space, with no smallness condition. For the usual nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation with decaying initial data, a mass-energy argument is used to preclude finite-time blow-up. Here both mass and total energy are infinite, but we put together a renormalized version of that bound by using the net mass transfer and the kinetic energy, which we show are a priori bounded. Global well-posedness on the energy space and on $1+H^1$ follows. We also treat a variant of the equation with a smooth real density response to show how this construction can be generalized to…

items.title: Effective bounds for adjoint Bloch-Kato Selmer groups of Hilbert modular forms
items.summary: Let $F$ be a totally real field and let $\Pi$ be a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb A_F)$. Under the usual Taylor-Wiles residual irreducibility hypothesis, we prove the vanishing of the adjoint Bloch-Kato Selmer group with characteristic-zero coefficients and give an explicit upper bound for a corresponding Selmer group with divisible coefficients. The argument revisits Wiles's use of level raising at Taylor-Wiles primes. In place of freeness or almost freeness of automorphic cohomology over a Hecke algebra, we compare congruence modules at the original and auxiliary levels and control the part of the Hecke cotangent space detected by the…

items.title: Understanding Failure Patterns in LLM-Based Mathematical Optimization Modeling
items.summary: Industrial optimization involves complex constraints, making optimization modeling difficult to automate. Large language models (LLMs) have been explored for generating optimization models from natural language, but their reliability in end-to-end settings remains limited, often producing non-executable, infeasible, or feasible but incorrect solutions. In this work, we study failure modes in LLM-based optimization modeling by decomposing the process into three components: mathematical reasoning, solver usage, and domain knowledge, and constructing datasets that target each aspect. Using these datasets, we analyze how different components relate to errors and find that they are associated…

items.summary: The quasinormal modes (QNMs) of a black hole are defined by keeping only ingoing waves at the horizon. We ask what horizon regularity requires of the outgoing waves this condition discards. We call these the horizon modes. For Schwarzschild black holes and the dominant $\ell=m=2$ Kerr modes, only the fundamental QNM decays more slowly than $\kappa$. These…

items.title: Comodule algebras and the cohomology of symplectic groups
items.summary: We prove that the homology of symplectic groups with Steinberg module coefficients forms a comodule algebra over the homology of general linear groups with Steinberg module coefficients. We prove a freeness-type result for comodule algebras. We deduce new lower bounds for the high-dimensional cohomology of symplectic groups of number rings and their congruence subgroups.

items.title: Scaling limits for products of induced symplectic Ginibre matrices

items.title: Worldsheet Effective Theory of Abelian-Higgs Cosmic Strings beyond Nambu--Goto

We derive a covariant worldsheet theory of their coupled dynamics directly from the Abelian-Higgs model at critical coupling, with all interaction coefficients fixed by the microscopic theory. The resulting action, which we validate against numerical lattice field theory simulations, extends the Nambu--Goto description to include a massive scalar shape mode and a massive vector mode. items.title: Majorana dark matter from a thick-to-thin brane junction: Modal stability, real-mediator coannihilation, and a dark-radiation imprint
items.summary: We show that the localized spectrum of a $D=7$ thick-to-thin brane junction can host a thermal Majorana dark-matter candidate.
